title: Rabbi Ami the Physician
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.2.3.11), folio 13b in Hyman’s citation, Rabbi Yonah asks a question and Rabbi Ami Asya reports Rabbi Yirmeyah’s ruling. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=567&lang=en) explains that Rabbi Ami said that (Rabbi) Assi ruled, and what he ruled is what Rabbi Yirmeyah said. Hyman rejects this, arguing that Rabbi Yirmeyah was Rabbi Zeira’s student, and Rabbi Zeira too was junior to Rabbi Ami.

Hyman suggests that the reading should be “Rabbi Ami his son-in-law,” and he is Rabbi Ami (II), who was Rabbi Yonah’s son-in-law. Likewise we find in the Jerusalem Talmud, end of Avodah Zarah, that Rabbi Ami asked Rabbi Yirmeyah.

notes.text: The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2:3 directly reads Ami Asya reporting that Yirmeyah ruled. Hyman’s proposed “his son-in-law,” the Ami (II) identification and the chronology argument remain conjectural identifications.

[Heilprin’s Ami entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=567&lang=en) records two explanations: that Assi ruled, and that Asya describes Ami as a physician. Guggenheimer adopts the physician reading in [Berakhot 2:3:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.2.3.11). Hyman’s “his son-in-law” is a further proposal.
